calibration.reference_10: Seeing Theory (Brown University) — the field's reference statistics explainer; in 'Sampling Distributions' the learner watches hundreds of sample means pile into a distribution and can vary n continuously, so bias-vs-variance is seen, not asserted, and every control is keyboard-operable at every width.
calibration.reference_8: BBC Bitesize GCSE 'Misleading graphs' / 'Sampling' revision pages carrying GOV.UK Design System accessibility: two-colour authored focus indicator, every chart with a legend and a table, focusable and named scroll regions, tables that reflow on a phone, and copy a 15-year-old reads without effort.

verdict: All three round-1 items are genuinely fixed: the A1 chart is full-width with a title band, collision-free end labels, a legend and no CSS wedge; the focus ring is a documented two-colour system (13.3:1 on paper, 15.3:1 on white, inverting in the header); and each activity now refuses to complete without the experiment (two axis ranges, both sample methods, the within-season view, a 15-character justification, a saved headline). It reads like a real investigation, never patronises or shames, and a 15-year-old on a 360 px phone can finish it one-handed in one sitting. But the screen-reader and keyboard path is not yet complete — the chart tables are unnamed scroll regions that Firefox/Safari keyboard users cannot scroll, and feedback that asks for an action or reveals a new question leaves focus where it was — so it sits at the top of the 7 rung, not yet the 8.

carry_over.evidence: app.js:116-117 sets viewBox to the measured width with a T=40 title band and R=60 end-label room; app.js:129 axis title at y=24 above the plot; app.js:135 fill:'none' plus styles.css:126 .chart polyline{fill:none} kills the wedge; app.js:139-145 pushes end labels apart (minGap 24/20) inside the viewBox; legend at app.js:146-148; tick/end-label sizes 14-16px (styles.css:129-132). shot-a1-framing-mobile/tablet/desktop show the chart at full card width with readable, non-overlapping 73.6/71.6 labels, a legend, and no filled wedges.

styles.css:21 --focus is #0f2a46 (13.3:1 on paper, 15.3:1 on white); styles.css:50-52 is the two-colour ring — 3px navy-deep outline + 3px #fff halo on light surfaces, inverting to white outline + navy-deep halo inside .top; TEST_REPORT.md:75 documents all three ratios under WCAG 1.4.11. No orange focus remains.

app.js:326 gates the A3 answer on the within-season view being used; app.js:327-330 blocks the keyed answer until the justification is ≥15 chars and moves focus to #a3-justify; app.js:331-334 sets answered only with justification; app.js:395 enables Finish only when answered && headlineSaved. app.js:266-268 gates the A2 answer on both methods being drawn. index.html:170-172 makes the correct A2 option no longer the longest (the 'noise' distractor is), and index.html:216-219 has the A3 options at comparable length.

blocking.issue: The chart data tables are horizontal scroll regions with no accessible name and no focusable element, so sighted keyboard users on Firefox/Safari cannot scroll to the off-screen columns (the A2 table is 7 columns wide at 360 px) and screen readers meet an unnamed region.
blocking.where: styles.css:148-149 (table{min-width:420px} inside .table-wrap{overflow-x:auto}); index.html:88 (#a1-table), index.html:164 (#a2-table), index.html:210 (#a3-table) have no tabindex/role/aria-label
blocking.why_it_caps_score: The brief requires a readable text/table alternative to every chart and keyboard access to every core action; a GOV.UK audit fails an unnamed, unfocusable scroll region, so 'keyboard-only and screen-reader paths are complete' is not yet true.

blocking.issue: When feedback asks for an action or a new question is revealed, focus stays on the Check button: 'Draw first, then decide.' leaves the Draw button a screen above on mobile, 'Look inside the seasons first.' leaves the season switch above, and the A1 follow-up question appears with no announcement (the focus call targets an h3 with no tabindex, so it does nothing).
blocking.where: app.js:186 ($('#a1-reflect h3').focus?.() — no tabindex, no announcement); app.js:268 (A2 early exit); app.js:326 (A3 early exit)
blocking.why_it_caps_score: The 8 bar says the keyboard-only and screen-reader paths are complete and the next action is always obvious; on a phone a learner is told to act on a control that is off-screen, and a screen reader is never told the follow-up question exists.

non_blocking.issue: The summary 'One limitation' placeholder is clipped at two rows on 360 px, so the example guidance is cut mid-sentence ('…rests on just 14–20 weeks' is partly hidden).
non_blocking.fix:
Shorten the placeholder to placeholder="e.g. One fictional year, one town; the season bands were our choice" and, if the full example matters, add it as a

under the textarea.

non_blocking.issue: #a2-table renders as an empty bordered sliver before any draw is made.
non_blocking.fix:
Add the hidden attribute in the markup (
) and in renderA2 set $('#a2-table').hidden = draws.length === 0; before filling it.

non_blocking.issue: The completed state of the progress steps is conveyed only visually (CSS ✓ and border colour, styles.css:69-70); the nav buttons keep the same accessible name for done and not-done.
non_blocking.fix: In go()'s step loop add: b.setAttribute('aria-label', `${b.textContent.trim()}${isDone(b.dataset.go) && !isCur ? ' — completed' : ''}`);

keep: The chart rendering system: viewBox set to the measured width (app.js:53, 116-117) so 1 SVG unit = 1 CSS px and the authored 14–16 px text is the real size at every viewport, with collision-pushed end labels, a title band and a legend (app.js:129-148, styles.css:126-138) — verified in shot-a1-framing-mobile/tablet/desktop.

The two-colour authored focus ring with documented ratios (styles.css:21, 50-52): navy-deep outline + white halo on light surfaces, white outline + navy-deep halo inside .top, with the numbers in TEST_REPORT.md:75 — the exact pattern GOV.UK uses.

Feedback that names the misconception in the learner's own numbers and never shames: 'The zoomed view didn't invent a difference; it magnified a real, small one' (app.js:184), 'A bigger convenience sample just estimates that group more precisely' (app.js:270), and 'there's no limit' on retries (app.js:191).

The experiment gates that make each activity real: two axis ranges before the A1 check (app.js:179), both sample methods drawn before the A2 answer (app.js:266-268), the within-season view before the A3 answer (app.js:326) plus the ≥15-character justification (app.js:327) and finish gated on answered && headlineSaved (app.js:395).

The accessibility foundation: skip link first in tab order (index.html:20), header/nav/main/footer landmarks, a body-level role=status announcer for every state change (app.js:67-69, 173, 258, 319), and prefers-reduced-motion switching off all animation and transition (styles.css:186).
gap_to_10: Seeing Theory (Brown), 'Sampling Distributions': the learner can vary n continuously and watch hundreds of sample means accumulate into a distribution, so the bias-vs-variance mechanism is demonstrated by the visual itself; Data Detective shows one dot per draw against the population line and states the mechanism in feedback, so the deepest idea is told rather than seen — that, plus GOV.UK-level completeness (named focusable scroll regions, every reveal announced), is the distance to the 10 rung.
